idea: CoffeeGuard is a voice-first reporting and triage system for coffee cooperatives battling coffee rust, where farmers call a local number and describe symptoms, and the system classifies, geotags, and alerts technicians with a severity score.

selected_gap.title: Structured Voice-Based Reporting and Classification
selected_gap.pain: Smallholder farmers lack a systematic way to report field problems. They rely on chaotic WhatsApp groups or manual notebooks, leading to lost reports, no classification, and delayed response.
selected_gap.why_now: Advances in speech-to-text and NLP for low-resource languages, combined with widespread use of basic phones with voice messaging, make it feasible to build a voice-first interface.
selected_gap.evidence_needed: Interview 20 farmers to quantify time spent in current methods, error rates, and willingness to use voice. Assess accuracy of transcription in target languages.
selected_gap.risk: User adoption of voice interface, accuracy in noisy farm environments, and convincing farmers to switch from familiar WhatsApp.

friedman_scores.note: No information about founder background; typical team lacks domain expertise in coffee agriculture.
Coffee cooperative market is large globally, but segment is fragmented and smallholder-focused; TAM likely in hundreds of millions.
Coffee rust is devastating; current manual reporting leads to significant yield losses; urgency is high.
WhatsApp and some agri apps exist, but no dominant voice-based solution for cooperatives; moderate competition.
No indication of founder's personal connection to coffee farmers or rust problem.
Advances in low-resource language speech-to-text and NLP make voice-based classification feasible for smallholder contexts.
Few successful voice-first agri-tech startups; Plantix (image-based) is a partial proxy but not voice.
Requires long-term partnership with cooperatives and trust-building; founder must be committed for years.
Voice interface can scale across languages, but requires localization and handling of noisy environments; moderate scalability.
Agri-tech for climate-resilient crops is a promising space, especially with AI for low-resource settings.

yc_rule_scores.criterion: Do not wait for the perfect idea
yc_rule_scores.note: The idea addresses a clear pain point; it's good enough to start validating quickly.
Focused on one idea; no distraction from other concepts.
Replaces chaotic WhatsApp notes with structured voice reporting; deeply integrated into farmer/technician workflow.

yc_rule_scores.criterion: Build at the edge of AI
yc_rule_scores.note: Uses NLP for low-resource languages; model improvements will directly enhance classification.
Value proposition is reduced yield loss and faster response, not just a reporting tool.
Ambitious to cover all coffee cooperatives; but scope is manageable initially.
Misclassifications can provide data to improve taxonomy; but not explicitly designed for that.
Coffee rust expertise is specialized; cooperatives are low-trust but high need; voice system can build trust.
The structured reporting process itself becomes the product; farmers adopt it as standard practice.
Risk of false positive interest from cooperatives; need to verify willingness to pay.
Can price per report or per cooperative subscription; aligns with outcome-based pricing.
Costs include phone calls, transcription, and SMS; need to keep low especially in low-margin agriculture.

yc_rule_scores.criterion: Do not bolt AI onto legacy
yc_rule_scores.note: Replaces manual WhatsApp notes with AI-native voice system; not bolting onto legacy.

yc_rule_scores.criterion: Cover domain, model, and operations fluency
yc_rule_scores.note: Requires coffee disease domain expertise, NLP model fluency, and field operations understanding.

vc_rubric_scores.rationale: No evidence of founder background in agriculture or NLP; typical team lacks unique advantage.
TAM for coffee cooperatives is large but fragmented; growth tied to climate pressures; timing is right.
Defensible moat is limited; voice data and taxonomy can be replicated; network effects weak.
No evidence of user interviews, pilots, or letters of intent; pure concept stage.
LTV:CAC unknown; subscription per cooperative likely low margins; no pricing validated.
Main competitor is manual WhatsApp; some agri-tech apps but none focused on voice; moderate threat from incumbents.
No financial data; assumed lean but burn rate not justified; runway unknown.
Key risks: farmer adoption, transcription accuracy in noisy fields, and reliance on phone networks; manageable but significant.

decision: Do not pursue at this stage; requires stronger founder-market fit and initial traction evidence.
next_experiments: Conduct 20 farmer interviews to quantify pain and willingness to use voice-based reporting.
Run a pilot with one cooperative to test transcription accuracy and classification in local languages.
Build a simple MVP using Twilio voice and a basic NLP model to validate workflow feasibility.
kill_criteria: Fewer than 50% of farmers express interest in switching from WhatsApp to voice system.
Transcription accuracy falls below 70% for key disease terms in target languages.
Cooperatives unwilling to pay even a nominal fee for the service.
_iteration_one_liner: We turn chaotic farmer voice notes into structured, triaged disease alerts for coffee cooperative technicians using a simple phone call.
